import statistics

# Data from Table 1 - Money in Circulation, "Paper money > Total paper money" column
# Using the 1950 bulletin for years 1943-1950 (latest revision), 1948 bulletin for 1941-1942 (not in 1950 bulletin)
# FY 1941-1950: 10 data points

# Values in millions of dollars
# From 1948 bulletin: 1941, 1942
# From 1950 bulletin: 1943-1950 (latest data, some values revised)
paper_money = [
    8932,   # 1941 (from 1948 bulletin - not in 1950)
    11600,  # 1942 (from 1948 bulletin - not in 1950)
    16492,  # 1943 (from 1950 bulletin)
    21438,  # 1944 (from 1950 bulletin)
    25511,  # 1945 (from 1950 bulletin - revised from 25541)
    26945,  # 1946 (from 1950 bulletin)
    26942,  # 1947 (from 1950 bulletin)
    26182,  # 1948 (from 1950 bulletin - revised from 26482)
    26034,  # 1949 (from 1950 bulletin)
    25661,  # 1950 (from 1950 bulletin)
]

print("Paper money values (millions):", paper_money)
print("Number of years:", len(paper_money))

# Calculate mean
mean_val = statistics.mean(paper_money)
print(f"Mean: {mean_val}")

# Sample standard deviation (n-1 denominator)
stdev = statistics.stdev(paper_money)
print(f"Stdev (sample): {stdev}")

# Calculate excess kurtosis using Fisher-Pearson bias-corrected formula
n = len(paper_money)
# Formula: ((n*(n+1))/((n-1)*(n-2)*(n-3))) * sum(((x-mean)/s)**4) - 3*(n-1)**2/((n-2)*(n-3))
s = stdev

# Calculate the sum of (x-mean)/s ^ 4
sum_fourth_moments = sum(((x - mean_val) / s) ** 4 for x in paper_money)
print(f"Sum of fourth moments: {sum_fourth_moments}")

# Calculate the two terms
term1 = (n * (n + 1)) / ((n - 1) * (n - 2) * (n - 3)) * sum_fourth_moments
term2 = 3 * (n - 1) ** 2 / ((n - 2) * (n - 3))

excess_kurtosis = term1 - term2
print(f"Term1: {term1}")
print(f"Term2: {term2}")
print(f"Fisher excess kurtosis: {excess_kurtosis}")

# Round to thousandths
rounded = round(excess_kurtosis, 3)
print(f"Rounded to thousandths: {rounded}")
